The invention relates to an inserter for placing an intrauterine system in the uterus. The inserter includes a handle and an insertion tube connected to the handle. The insertion tube is designed to guide and position the intrauterine system during insertion.

The insertion tube has a first end and a second end. The first end is configured for introduction toward or into the uterus during use, while the second end is connected to, or associated with, the handle. The first end of the insertion tube includes at least one frame slot. The frame slot is configured to receive at least part of the frame of the intrauterine system, thereby helping to position, guide, or retain the frame during preparation and insertion.

The invention also relates to a kit comprising the inserter and an intrauterine system suitable for use with the inserter. The intrauterine system includes a therapeutic component and a continuous, closed frame. The frame is connected to the therapeutic component at one or more connection points. The therapeutic component may be configured to provide a therapeutic effect after placement in the uterus, for example by releasing an active agent.

In the kit, the intrauterine system is arranged relative to the insertion tube so that the therapeutic component is mainly positioned inside the first end of the insertion tube. At the same time, the continuous, closed frame is mainly positioned outside the first end of the insertion tube. The at least one frame slot at the first end of the insertion tube may receive a portion of the frame, allowing the frame to be held in a suitable position while leaving most of the frame outside the insertion tube.

This arrangement may facilitate loading, handling, and insertion of the intrauterine system. By positioning the therapeutic component primarily inside the insertion tube and the frame primarily outside the insertion tube, the inserter can help protect and guide the therapeutic component while allowing the frame to remain appropriately oriented for deployment within the uterus.

An intrauterine system inserter is provided for facilitating the placement and delivery of an intrauterine system into the uterus. The inserter includes a handle and an insertion tube extending from the handle. The insertion tube has a first end configured for introduction toward or through the cervix during use, and this first end is provided with at least one frame slot. The frame slot is shaped and positioned to receive a portion of a continuous closed frame of the intrauterine system.

The intrauterine system may include a therapeutic component, such as a drug-containing body, reservoir, capsule, or other active-agent delivery structure, connected to or supported by the continuous closed frame. In the assembled insertion arrangement, the therapeutic component is positioned primarily within the insertion tube, while the continuous closed frame is positioned primarily outside the insertion tube. At least part of the frame is received in the frame slot at the first end of the insertion tube, allowing the frame to be held in a controlled and organized position relative to the tube.

This configuration helps maintain the intrauterine system in a suitable orientation before and during insertion. By allowing the therapeutic component to remain mainly inside the insertion tube and the frame to remain mainly outside the insertion tube, the inserter can reduce twisting, folding, or misalignment of the system. The frame slot provides a defined receiving location for the frame, which assists in stabilizing the intrauterine system during loading, handling, and delivery.

During use, the intrauterine system is arranged with the therapeutic component inside the insertion tube and the continuous closed frame engaged with the at least one frame slot. The insertion tube is then advanced to the desired delivery position. Once properly positioned, the intrauterine system may be released from the inserter so that the therapeutic component and frame assume their intended placement within the uterus. The handle may be used to control advancement, positioning, and release of the intrauterine system.

The described inserter therefore provides an organized and reliable way to prepare and deliver an intrauterine system having a continuous closed frame. The cooperation between the frame slot and the frame helps ensure that the system is retained in a predictable arrangement before deployment, while the insertion tube protects and guides the therapeutic component during insertion. This arrangement may improve ease of use and support accurate placement of the intrauterine system.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style description of an invention relating to an intrauterine system inserter with numbered components, emphasizing the insertion tube’s first end having a frame slot and a kit comprising the inserter and IUS.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent-Style Description

### Title  
**Inserter for an Intrauterine System and Kit Comprising the Inserter and an Intrauterine System**

### Field of the Invention  
The invention relates to medical devices for placement of intrauterine systems within a uterine cavity. More particularly, the invention relates to an inserter for an intrauterine system, the inserter comprising an insertion tube having a first end configured to receive and protect at least part of the intrauterine system during insertion. The invention further relates to a kit comprising the inserter and an intrauterine system.

### Background  
Intrauterine systems are commonly inserted into the uterus using an inserter having a tubular member and an operating handle. During insertion, it is desirable that the intrauterine system be held in a predictable and stable orientation, while also being protected from deformation or unintended release. In particular, intrauterine systems having a frame, such as a generally T-shaped frame, may include transverse arms or other frame portions that must be aligned and accommodated within the inserter prior to deployment.

There remains a need for an inserter that reliably receives the frame of an intrauterine system at a distal or uterine-facing end of an insertion tube and facilitates controlled delivery of the intrauterine system into the uterine cavity.

### Summary of the Invention  
According to one aspect, an inserter for an intrauterine system is provided. The inserter comprises an insertion tube having a first end and a second end. The first end is configured for introduction through the cervix toward the uterine cavity. The first end of the insertion tube comprises a frame slot configured to receive at least a portion of a frame of an intrauterine system.

In certain embodiments, the frame slot is formed as an opening, recess, cut-out, channel, or longitudinally extending slot at the first end of the insertion tube. The frame slot may be dimensioned to receive a transverse frame portion, arm portion, stem portion, or junction region of the intrauterine system. The frame slot may assist in maintaining the intrauterine system in a defined rotational orientation relative to the insertion tube.

According to another aspect, a kit is provided. The kit comprises an inserter and an intrauterine system. The inserter comprises an insertion tube having a first end provided with a frame slot, and the intrauterine system comprises a frame configured to be at least partially received in the frame slot prior to or during insertion.

### Brief Description of the Components  
The following reference numerals may be used in the description:

- **1** Inserter  
- **2** Intrauterine system  
- **3** Insertion tube  
- **4** First end of the insertion tube  
- **5** Second end of the insertion tube  
- **6** Frame slot  
- **7** Handle  
- **8** Slider or actuator  
- **9** Plunger or inner member  
- **10** Depth indicator or flange  
- **11** Frame of the intrauterine system  
- **12** Stem of the frame  
- **13** Transverse arm portion  
- **14** Hormone reservoir or body portion  
- **15** Removal thread  
- **16** Longitudinal axis of the insertion tube  
- **17** Distal opening of the insertion tube  
- **18** Slot edge  
- **19** Slot base  
- **20** Package or sterile enclosure  

### Detailed Description  
An inserter **1** for an intrauterine system **2** comprises an insertion tube **3** extending along a longitudinal axis **16**. The insertion tube **3** has a first end **4** and a second end **5**. The first end **4** is a distal end intended to be advanced toward or into the uterine cavity during use. The second end **5** may be connected to or associated with a handle **7**.

The inserter **1** further comprises an actuator, such as a slider **8**, arranged to control movement of the intrauterine system **2** relative to the insertion tube **3**. In one embodiment, the inserter **1** comprises a plunger or inner member **9** movable relative to the insertion tube **3**. The plunger **9** may support, push, retain, or deploy the intrauterine system **2** when the actuator **8** is operated.

The insertion tube **3** comprises, at its first end **4**, a frame slot **6**. The frame slot **6** is configured to receive at least part of a frame **11** of the intrauterine system **2**. The frame slot **6** may extend from a distal opening **17** of the insertion tube **3** in a direction generally parallel to the longitudinal axis **16**. Alternatively, the frame slot **6** may extend obliquely, circumferentially, or partially circumferentially, depending on the shape of the frame **11** to be accommodated.

In one embodiment, the frame slot **6** is defined by opposed slot edges **18** and a slot base **19**. The opposed slot edges **18** may guide a portion of the frame **11** into a predetermined position. The slot base **19** may limit proximal movement of the frame portion into the slot **6** and thereby define a loading position of the intrauterine system **2** relative to the insertion tube **3**.

The intrauterine system **2** may comprise a frame **11** having a stem **12** and a transverse arm portion **13**. The stem **12** may support a body portion, such as a hormone reservoir **14**. One or more removal threads **15** may extend from the intrauterine system **2**. Prior to insertion, at least a portion of the frame **11**, for example the transverse arm portion **13** or a junction between the transverse arm portion **13** and the stem **12**, may be received in the frame slot **6**.

The frame slot **6** at the first end **4** of the insertion tube **3** provides a defined receiving region for the frame **11**. By receiving a part of the frame **11**, the frame slot **6** may reduce undesired twisting, bending, or displacement of the intrauterine system **2** during loading and insertion. The frame slot **6** may also help maintain the intrauterine system **2** in a selected angular orientation relative to the insertion tube **3**, thereby facilitating controlled deployment.

In some embodiments, the first end **4** of the insertion tube **3** is shaped to provide atraumatic insertion. The edges surrounding the frame slot **6** may be rounded, chamfered, polished, or otherwise configured to reduce tissue irritation. The insertion tube **3** may be made of a polymeric material suitable for medical use, such as polyethylene, polypropylene, polyamide, polyurethane, or another biocompatible material. The frame slot **6** may be formed by cutting, molding, machining, laser processing, or any other suitable manufacturing method.

The inserter **1** may further comprise a depth indicator or flange **10** arranged on the insertion tube **3**. The depth indicator **10** may be movable along the insertion tube **3** to indicate the uterine sounding depth and assist in positioning the first end **4** of the insertion tube **3** at a desired insertion depth.

During use, the intrauterine system **2** is positioned relative to the inserter **1** such that at least part of its frame **11** is received in the frame slot **6** at the first end **4** of the insertion tube **3**. The first end **4** of the insertion tube **3** is then advanced through the cervical canal. When the intrauterine system **2** is located at a desired position, the actuator **8** is operated to cause relative movement between the insertion tube **3** and the intrauterine system **2**, thereby releasing the frame **11** from the frame slot **6** and deploying the intrauterine system **2** in the uterine cavity.

### Kit  
A kit according to the invention comprises the inserter **1** and the intrauterine system **2**. The inserter **1** comprises the insertion tube **3** having the first end **4** with the frame slot **6**. The intrauterine system **2** comprises the frame **11**, at least part of which is configured to be received in the frame slot **6**.

The kit may further comprise a sterile package **20** enclosing the inserter **1** and the intrauterine system **2**. In one embodiment, the intrauterine system **2** is preloaded in the inserter **1**, with a portion of the frame **11** positioned in the frame slot **6**. In another embodiment, the intrauterine system **2** is supplied separately within the same kit and is loadable into the inserter **1** before use.

The kit may additionally include instructions for use, a uterine sound, gloves, antiseptic materials, or other accessories suitable for insertion of the intrauterine system **2**.

### Exemplary Claims-Style Statements  
1. An inserter **1** for an intrauterine system **2**, comprising an insertion tube **3** having a first end **4** and a second end **5**, wherein the first end **4** comprises a frame slot **6** configured to receive at least a portion of a frame **11** of the intrauterine system **2**.

2. The inserter of statement 1, wherein the frame slot **6** extends from a distal opening **17** of the insertion tube **3** in a direction generally parallel to a longitudinal axis **16** of the insertion tube **3**.

3. The inserter of statement 1 or 2, wherein the frame slot **6** is configured to receive a transverse arm portion **13** of the frame **11**.

4. The inserter of any preceding statement, further comprising a handle **7** connected to the second end **5** of the insertion tube **3**.

5. The inserter of any preceding statement, further comprising an actuator **8** configured to deploy the intrauterine system **2** from the insertion tube **3**.

6. The inserter of any preceding statement, wherein the frame slot **6** is configured to maintain the intrauterine system **2** in a predetermined rotational orientation relative to the insertion tube **3**.

7. A kit comprising the inserter **1** of any preceding statement and an intrauterine system **2** having a frame **11**, wherein at least a portion of the frame **11** is configured to be received in the frame slot **6**.

8. The kit of statement 7, wherein the intrauterine system **2** is preloaded in the inserter **1**.

9. The kit of statement 7 or 8, further comprising a sterile package **20** enclosing the inserter **1** and the intrauterine system **2**.

### European Patent Claim Summary

**Independent device claim (summary):**  
An inserter for positioning an intrauterine system in the uterus, the inserter comprising a **handle (3)** and an **insertion tube (6)** connected to or operable from the handle. The insertion tube is configured to receive and guide an **intrauterine system (1)** comprising a **therapeutic component (1b)** connected to a **continuous closed frame (1a)**. The inserter includes **at least one frame slot** arranged to receive or accommodate a portion of the continuous closed frame during loading, storage, or insertion, thereby assisting in maintaining, guiding, constraining, or orienting the intrauterine system for delivery through the insertion tube and subsequent deployment in the uterus.

**Key claim features:**

1. **Inserter structure**
   - A handle (3) for manipulating the inserter.
   - An insertion tube (6) extending from the handle.
   - At least one frame slot associated with the inserter, preferably with the insertion tube or a distal portion thereof.

2. **Intrauterine system**
   - An intrauterine system (1) receivable in the inserter.
   - The intrauterine system includes:
     - a continuous closed frame (1a); and
     - a therapeutic component (1b) connected to the frame.

3. **Functional relationship**
   - The frame slot is configured to accommodate part of the continuous closed frame (1a).
   - The slot facilitates controlled loading, retention, guidance, or deployment of the intrauterine system.
   - The insertion tube (6) is configured to deliver the intrauterine system into the uterus.

**Possible dependent claim concepts:**

- The at least one frame slot is formed in a wall of the insertion tube (6).  
- The frame slot extends longitudinally along at least part of the insertion tube.  
- Two opposed frame slots are provided for receiving opposite portions of the closed frame.  
- The continuous closed frame (1a) is elastically deformable between an insertion configuration and a deployed configuration.  
- The therapeutic component (1b) comprises a drug reservoir, hormone-releasing element, copper-containing element, or other active therapeutic portion.  
- The handle (3) includes an actuator for moving the insertion tube relative to the intrauterine system.  
- The frame slot prevents twisting or improper orientation of the intrauterine system during insertion.  
- The inserter is preloaded with the intrauterine system.  
- The closed frame (1a) is substantially annular, polygonal, oval, loop-shaped, or otherwise continuous in shape.  

**Example claim-style formulation:**  
An inserter for an intrauterine system, comprising a handle (3), an insertion tube (6), and at least one frame slot, wherein the insertion tube is configured to receive an intrauterine system (1) comprising a therapeutic component (1b) connected to a continuous closed frame (1a), and wherein the at least one frame slot is arranged to accommodate a portion of the continuous closed frame so as to guide or retain the intrauterine system during insertion and deployment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into formal patent language: a contraceptive intrauterine system inserter where the frame remains mostly outside the insertion tube while the therapeutic component is mostly inside it.
counterfactuals.output:
An intrauterine system inserter for introducing a contraceptive intrauterine system into a uterus, the intrauterine system comprising a frame portion and a therapeutic component carried by or associated with the frame portion, wherein the inserter comprises an elongate insertion tube having a distal end configured for uterine insertion and a proximal end configured for manipulation by a user, and wherein, in a pre-insertion configuration, the frame portion of the intrauterine system is disposed substantially outside the insertion tube while the therapeutic component is disposed substantially within the insertion tube.

In one embodiment, the frame portion comprises one or more laterally extending arms or resilient structural members adapted to assume an expanded configuration after placement in the uterus. The therapeutic component may comprise a hormone-releasing reservoir, drug-containing body, medicament carrier, sleeve, capsule, or other active substance delivery element. The insertion tube is dimensioned and arranged to receive and protect at least a major portion of the therapeutic component during insertion, while at least a major portion of the frame portion remains external to the insertion tube prior to deployment.

The inserter may further comprise a pusher, plunger, rod, handle, slider, or other actuation member configured to advance the therapeutic component and/or the intrauterine system relative to the insertion tube. The insertion tube may be withdrawn relative to the intrauterine system, or the intrauterine system may be advanced relative to the insertion tube, to deploy the contraceptive intrauterine system within the uterus. The arrangement in which the frame remains substantially outside the insertion tube and the therapeutic component remains substantially inside the insertion tube may facilitate reduced insertion-tube diameter, protection of the therapeutic component, simplified loading, and controlled placement of the contraceptive intrauterine system.

**Exemplary claim language**

1. An inserter for a contraceptive intrauterine system, the contraceptive intrauterine system comprising a frame and a therapeutic component, the inserter comprising:  
   an insertion tube defining a lumen and having a distal insertion end; and  
   an actuator configured to deploy the contraceptive intrauterine system from the insertion tube;  
   wherein, before deployment, a major portion of the therapeutic component is positioned within the lumen of the insertion tube and a major portion of the frame is positioned outside the lumen of the insertion tube.

2. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the frame comprises at least one resilient arm configured to expand after placement of the contraceptive intrauterine system in a uterus.

3. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the therapeutic component comprises a drug-releasing reservoir.

4. The inserter of claim 3, wherein the drug-releasing reservoir comprises a contraceptive hormone.

5. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the insertion tube is configured to shield the therapeutic component during insertion while leaving at least part of the frame exposed externally of the insertion tube.

6. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the actuator comprises a pusher member movable relative to the insertion tube.

7. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the insertion tube is retractable relative to the contraceptive intrauterine system to deploy the therapeutic component from the lumen.

8. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the frame is retained in a pre-deployment configuration outside the insertion tube prior to insertion.

9. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the therapeutic component is elongate and extends axially within the lumen of the insertion tube.

10. The inserter of claim 1, wherein the frame and the therapeutic component are connected to form a unitary intrauterine system deployable from the inserter.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a concise patent specification excerpt beginning “The present invention relates to…” for an inserter and kit used with an intrauterine system having a closed frame and therapeutic component.
counterfactuals.output:
The present invention relates to an inserter and kit for positioning an intrauterine system within a uterine cavity, the intrauterine system comprising a closed frame carrying or retaining a therapeutic component. The inserter comprises an elongate insertion tube having a distal receiving portion configured to accommodate the closed frame in a compressed delivery configuration, a handle at a proximal end, and an actuator operable to advance or release the intrauterine system from the distal receiving portion. The insertion tube is dimensioned for transcervical introduction and is configured to shield the closed frame during insertion.

In one embodiment, the closed frame is resiliently deformable between the compressed delivery configuration and an expanded deployed configuration, and the therapeutic component comprises a drug reservoir, hormone-releasing body, copper-containing element, or other active agent carrier coupled to the frame. Upon actuation, the frame exits the distal receiving portion and returns toward the expanded deployed configuration, thereby positioning the therapeutic component within the uterine cavity.

The kit comprises the inserter, the intrauterine system preloaded in the distal receiving portion or provided separately for loading, and sterile packaging. The kit may further include a depth gauge, cervical stop, deployment indicator, instructions for use, and one or more replacement or alternative therapeutic components. The inserter and kit provide controlled placement of a closed-frame intrauterine system while reducing handling of the therapeutic component prior to insertion.
